newsitem.title: FINLAND: Yeltsin says Russia prepared to join EU.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says Russia prepared to join EU.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin said on Saturday Moscow was prepared to join the European Union as part of its drive to be integrated into Europe.

"(Russia) is also aiming to be recognised finally as a full European state and we are also prepared to join the European Union," he told reporters after a meeting with Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari.
Russia and the EU have signed a partnership and cooperation agreement designed to forge commercial and other links and to liberalise trade. But the deal has not been fully ratified.
The EU has promised 10 other former eastern bloc countries eventual membership but does not see the trade agreement with Russia as leading towards its joining the 15-nation body.

Yeltsin was speaking a day after a summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton at which the two sides agreed to push for Moscow's membership of a number of world economic bodies, including the Paris Club of government creditors and the World Trade Organisation.
Russia opposes NATO's plans to invite former Soviet states to join but is far less concerned about them becoming EU members.
